speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with a low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To help narrow down the cause, how long have these symptoms been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19. The clinical presentation of a "slapped cheek" facial rash followed by a pruritic lacy rash on the trunk and extremities, preceded by viral prodromal symptoms in a school-aged child, is classic for this condition.
